Q_definition: Q_s is the sum over the three perfect matchings of K4 of the two selected block entries, one selected clone at each site

dominance.conclusion: The polynomial map from six arbitrary 2x2 blocks to Q is dominant. Hence Q satisfies no universal nonzero polynomial identity such as a matchgate quadric.

four_tensor_covariance.conclusion: Independent GL2 changes at the four supervertices act on Q as an ordinary four-qubit tensor.
four_tensor_covariance.representation: V0 tensor V1 tensor V2 tensor V3

must_fire: support8 even Cartan expression is exactly 4

nearest_applicable_theorem.negative_test: The arity-four matchgate/pure-spinor characterization: definite parity plus the single Cartan quadric is necessary and sufficient in a nonzero chart. It excludes both frozen examples rather than furnishing an identity for Q.
nearest_applicable_theorem.paired_pfaffian_caution: Proposition 1.2 of notes/pairwise-matchgate-compatibility.md applies to a full normalized transversal chart as a paired restriction of a 2n-node Pfaffian signature; it does not turn this signless Hafnian Q into a standard four-bit matchgate signature.
nearest_applicable_theorem.positive_structure: Q is an ordinary four-qubit covariant. General four-qubit tensor invariant/SLOCC theory applies, but dominance means it provides invariants, not universal vanishing equations.

scope_guard: This classifies Q itself. It does not rule out a source-relative paired-Pfaffian identity retaining the six block matrices or other lower-sector data.
